definition: A Rust Query obtains owned Entity snapshots through one declared read-only asynchronous trait dependency, then applies the authored filter, stable ordering, limit and projection without persistence or mutation.
dependency: Each Query owns a dedicated Reader trait. Its async read method receives the Query's borrowed explicit parameters and returns Result<Vec<SourceEntity>, QueryError>. Generated code neither opens storage nor chooses a provider.
result: The Query consumes the returned row vector and produces owned immutable projection structs. Cloning is restricted to this explicit owned-output boundary and retains the declared native field type.
comparison: Equality uses native declared Eq. UInt64 and Bool use native order. String comparison uses UTF-16 code-unit lexicographic order to preserve the existing Query contract across targets. Ordering is stable and authored direction and limit are exact.
module: One collision-free module per qualified selector under src/application/queries, with exact imports derived from the checked source Entity.
verification: Deterministic planning, actual async provider execution under Cargo, filter/order/limit/projection observations and wrong-provider or wrong-type compile-fail controls are required.
compatibility: Existing source schemas and generators remain unchanged. This candidate is selected only by the reconciled Rust path and has no default cutover.
